messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Age: 34
Gender: Female
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
Patient with platin-resistant metastatic ovarian cancer was admitted to the hospital after experiencing fever and chills during infusion of nivolumab. Physical examination showed nausea and a known pelvic mass. Infusion was stopped and antihistamines and corticosteroids were administered. However, the patient remained febrile and was found to have a positive blood culture for bacillus Gram-positive bacteria. Combination therapy with antibiotics was started, but three blood cultures returned positive for rapidly growing mycobacteria. The port-a-cath was removed and antibiotics were switched to clarithromycin and ethambutol. Diagnosis of M. mucogenicum port-a-cath related bloodstream infection was retained.

Treatment and Management:
Patient received combination antibiotherapy for two months and antibiotics were pursued for six months. Despite concomitant chemotherapy, no relapse of infection was observed after antibiotic discontinuation.

Follow-up:
Patient was discharged in stable condition with instructions to continue chemotherapy and to monitor for any signs of infection.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Nontuberculous mycobacteria (M. mucogenicum) caused a bloodstream infection that started at the patient's port-a-cath. That infection is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. ICD-10-AM codes an infection caused by an implanted vascular access device as a device complication, which falls in chapter T (infection due to vascular devices, T82.7), with the organism and sepsis codes added as secondary codes.

CODE: T82
